title: HR
leads: Nobody. You hold every open seat, every onboarding file, and the handbook.
where: The Cairo office. Sites on launch day, for papers. Some work is remote
hours: Office days. Reachable the same day for a referral, a missing form, or housing
summary: You bring every new person in: screened, papers complete, day one signed, housed if needed.

posting.headline: HR (hiring, papers, and the handbook), Cairo
posting.about: We run video recording teams at factories, warehouses, farms, and construction sites across Cairo. Workers wear a small camera on a cap while they do their normal job. HR brings every new person into the company: operators, runners, reviewers, and office staff. You screen names, write the offer letters and contracts, and keep the handbook and this map. Nobody starts without you.
do: Take every referral and application. Screen the name in the same week.
Book the interview with the manager who owns the seat.
Write the offer letter and the contract. Collect the onboarding papers.
Keep every wearer's screening papers: ID copy, consent, fraud briefing, one account.
File the signed day-one sheet before the first shift.
Arrange housing for workers who come from another city to open a site.
Keep the employee handbook and this company map current.
Confirm each referred hire is working, so the hire reward is paid.
need: You have done hiring, contracts, or office paperwork in Egypt before.
Careful with paper. A missing ID or an unsigned form is yours to catch.
Clear and short in writing, in Arabic and English.
Warm on the phone with a nervous applicant, and firm about the rules.
plus: You have hired factory or warehouse workers in large numbers.
You have arranged housing or transport for a team.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
Every step of hiring is already written down. You run it.
A seat next to the people who run the company.
You keep the handbook. What you write is what everyone follows.
posting.apply: Send your name, where you live, a phone number, and the hiring work you have done. We call back within two working days.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of HR at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the Chief of Staff.
Your start date is {start}. In your first weeks you take over the onboarding files and the handbook from {manager}, and take one new hire from referral to first shift.

terms.label: Place of work
terms.v: The Cairo office. Sites on launch day, for papers. Some work is remote

terms.label: Hours
terms.v: Office days. Reachable the same day for a referral, a missing form, or housing

terms.label: Pay
terms.v: {pay} per month, paid at the end of the month

conditions: A copy of your national ID.
Your signature on the rules, the consent form, and the fraud briefing.
One account in your own name. Accounts are never shared.
expect: Nobody starts without complete papers, whoever recommended them.
Every referral gets an answer in the same week.
Every file you keep is complete, and you can find it the same day.
offer.closing: Please sign below to accept this offer. We look forward to working with you.

handbook.purpose: The client pays only for hours filmed by people with complete papers: ID copy, signed consent, signed fraud briefing, one account in their own name. You bring every new person in and keep those papers. An empty seat or a missing form is yours to fix.
outcomes: Everyone joins through you: screened, interviewed, papers complete, day one signed.
Every wearer has a full file before a phone goes on their head.
The handbook and this map say what we really do.
daily: Morning. Take every new referral and application. Screen each name this week.
Same day. Confirm and file every ID photo and form a Portfolio Manager sends.
Same day. A wearer with no file gets no phone until the file is complete.
Every day. Tell Mano where each open seat stands: screen, interview, papers, day one.
Before a first shift. The signed day-one sheet is in the onboarding file.
weekly: Once a week. Open seats with Mano. A short bench means hiring starts that week.
Portfolio review. Count housed seats. Each ends the day its local hire signs day one.
Once a week. Fix the handbook and this map for anything that changed.
monthly: Month end. Tell Ahmed Alaa which referred hires are working. He pays the hire reward.
Month end. Check every contract and probation date that ends next month.
standards: Nobody starts without papers, whoever recommended them. No ID, no phone.
Every referral is screened in the same week, or the referrer hears why not.
The manager who owns the seat does the interview. You book it.
No ID or under 18: tell Mano, then check every file on that site.
Housing only for a site that opens before local hiring is done.
When someone leaves, their file closes after all gear is back and checked.
never: Nobody starts, and nobody films, before every line of onboarding screening is done.
A removed worker never comes back, and an old account is never used again.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: Take over the onboarding files and the handbook from Mano.
Take one new hire from referral to day one.
Book an interview for every open seat. Handle one housing case with Mano.
Every file complete before a launch day. Mano signs you off.

measures: Days from referral to day one, for every hire.
Wearer files complete before launch day, every launch.
Referrals screened in the same week. Zero left waiting.
Housed seats, counted down to zero each week.
handbook.call: Mano for everything. Moharam for the bench, a first shift, or an incident. Ahmed Alaa for pay and hire rewards. When Mano is away, Moharam covers people, screening, and housing.
